# 0.15.153

**The phone: first run, and the navigation bar.**

Derek's first look at 0.15.152 on a real phone found three things the harness could not:

- **There was no first run.** A phone with no identity landed on an empty Messages panel with no
  way to settings, to a profile, to anything. The phone now has the desktop's three screens: make
  an identity (the username is claimed in the background, as on the desktop), the address the core
  actually holds with its QR code, and the recovery file — which on a phone is written into the
  app's own files and offered to the share sheet at once, because a file that stays on the phone is
  lost with it. Restoring from a recovery file and unlocking a sealed account are there too.
- **The navigation bar covered the bottom of everything.** The page draws under it, and the WebView
  reports no inset for it (it knows about a camera cutout and nothing else), so the user bar —
  your avatar, notifications, settings — sat behind the three buttons and every sheet's last row
  was under them. The shell now measures the real status bar and navigation bar on whatever phone
  it is on and tells the page; the keyboard shrinks the page above itself instead of covering it.
- **The back button** went through the WebView's history. It now goes to the app's own back — a
  sheet, a page, a conversation back to the drawer — and only steps the app aside when there is
  nothing left to go back from.

**Restoring a recovery file broke the next launch — on every device.** The restore wiped every
table, including the one that says which shape the database is, so the next open tried to migrate
a database that was already migrated and the app aborted before it drew anything ("duplicate
column name"). Found on Derek's phone the first time a recovery file was restored on it; the
desktop had the same fault. The marker now survives a restore, and a database that already lost
it opens instead of refusing to.

Also on the phone: the page could not reach its own core at all (the bridge the desktop's config
turns on was never turned on for the phone), so every earlier phone build was hollow; the phone's
username claim and relay lookups no longer panic (Android needs the app's context for DNS and its
own trust roots for HTTPS — both are now given); the whole app sits above the phone's button bar
as one block; the user bar is sized like the rows above it; and a first-run screen that ends
without an identity is shown again, never skipped.

Desktop: the restore fix above, and the repaint fix from 0.15.152.
